definition: Inner face — the I-consciousness (ahaṃtā) turned inward, made relishable (rasayati). In Spandasandoha, Śiva 'makes the inner face taste' — the self-awareness that is the spanda itself. Our identification with ahaṃtā is an inference, not Kṣemarāja's explicit statement.

sources.claim: yo'ntarvaktraṃ rasayati (who makes the inner face taste)
antarvaktra = I-consciousness (ahaṃtā); identification is ours, not Kṣemarāja's explicit statement

translations.note: 'Inner face' is literal; 'I-consciousness' is the technical gloss. The term evokes the face turned inward, toward oneself.
